clue.text: Collect money, say, for a light

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is to be heard spoken, not spelt out

parts.note: to collect money is to win dough, dough being slang for cash

explanation.surface: Someone takes a fee in exchange for a light, perhaps a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals a sound-alike: WIN DOUGH, spoken, gives the word for a pane of glass in a wall. 'Light' is not illumination but the glazed opening itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A light is an old and architectural term for a glazed opening in a wall or roof.

clue.text: Playwright seen as rising short story writer

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards, that is backwards
short says the writer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote children's stories such as The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A dramatist is seen as a writer of short stories on the up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts NESBIT to NESBI; 'rising', in a down entry, turns it upwards to the Norwegian dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian author of A Doll's House, wrote for the stage.

clue.text: 2, for example, made a start amid riots

indicators.note: riots suggests wild disorder, so the letters of the words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer for the stage got going during civil unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' refers to the answer to 2 Down, a famous playwright. 'riots' scrambles START and AMID; 'made a' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen is an example of a writer of plays.

clue.text: Within themselves an intriguing lot

parts.note: plays on the idiom for hidden layers of scheming, where these things turn inside more of themselves

explanation.surface: A group of fascinating people keep themselves to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'X within X' describes a tangle of secret plots; 'intriguing' means plotting, not fascinating.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'wheels within wheels' describes concealed influences and plotting.

clue.text: It is difficult being so sensitive

explanation.surface: Someone excuses their touchiness by saying life is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: One word does both jobs: a delicate, awkward problem, and a person who squirms when touched.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky, delicate situation is described this way, and so is a person who reacts readily to being tickled.

clue.text: Would Wenscelaus looking out have seen such a novel character?

definitions.text: Would Wenscelaus looking out have seen such a novel character?

parts.words: Would Wenscelaus looking out have seen such a novel character?
parts.note: Good King Wenceslas looked out on deep crisp snow, so a figure out there would be clad in snow, and the phrase is also a Wilkie Collins title

explanation.surface: A carol's king glances out of the window and spots an odd person.
explanation.walkthrough: In the carol, Good King Wenceslas looks out on snow lying deep and crisp and even; anyone out there would be covered in it. Wilkie Collins's 1859 mystery novel has this title character.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Catherick, the mysterious figure in Wilkie Collins's 1859 sensation novel, is known by this description.

clue.text: Tom had a search in the vault

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Tom hunted around inside the strongroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground burial chamber or gallery is a kind of vault for the dead.

clue.text: Alter letters of more recent date

indicators.note: Alter letters asks us to shuffle the letters of the word alter itself

explanation.surface: Someone changes the dates on recent correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' points at the letters of 'Alter' itself, which are to be rearranged; 'Alter' looks like the instruction but is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coming afterwards in time is more recent than what preceded it.

clue.text: Perfunctory goodbye used by broadcasters

parts.note: a perfunctory reply is short, brief and curt
a wave of the hand is a goodbye

explanation.surface: Television presenters sign off with a curt farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio transmissions on high frequencies with long range, used by international broadcasters.

clue.text: Governor in control of the minutes

definitions.text: Governor in control of the minutes

parts.words: Governor in control of the minutes
parts.note: reads like a chairman managing a meeting's record, but means the clockwork part that regulates how fast time passes

explanation.surface: A committee chair takes charge of the meeting's written record.
explanation.walkthrough: The governor is a regulating mechanism, and the minutes are those a clock shows, not a meeting's notes.
explanation.definitionFit: In a clock or watch this mechanism regulates the release of the train of gears, governing timekeeping.

clue.text: Gadget to take in return

indicators.note: in return says the word for what is taken is read from back to front

parts.note: loot is what is taken, as plunder

explanation.surface: Someone is lent a gadget in exchange for a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small instrument or implement used for a job.

clue.text: Cut in design work?

parts.note: a design that is cut into a surface rather than raised from it, as on a seal or gem

explanation.definitionFit: This is engraving sunk below the surface of stone or metal, the opposite of relief carving.

clue.text: 'I was a pale young — then.' (The Sorcerer)

definitions.text: 'I was a pale young — then.' (The Sorcerer)

parts.words: 'I was a pale young — then.' (The Sorcerer)
parts.note: a line from a song in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Sorcerer, sung by the vicar Dr Daly, with his youthful church post missing

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: Dr Daly, the vicar in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Sorcerer, recalls his younger days as an assistant clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is a junior clergyman, an assistant to a parish priest, which Dr Daly once was.

clue.text: Given .a dowry, this beautiful creature would be a jewel

indicators.note: Given a dowry describes adding something, so the creature is the jewel with the dowry taken away

parts.note: a peridot is a green gemstone, a kind of olivine
dot is an old word for a dowry, from French

explanation.surface: A lovely woman, once given her marriage portion, becomes a prize catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards from the jewel: PERIDOT minus DOT, an old word for a dowry, leaves the fairy of Persian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian mythology a peri is a fairy or elf-like spirit of great beauty.

clue.text: Doolittle and March meet a royal person

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady
Beth March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women

explanation.surface: Two people named Doolittle and March are introduced to royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month or a parade; it is the surname of Beth in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Several queens, including the two English monarchs, have borne this first name.

clue.text: To do with charges for heraldry

definitions.text: To do with charges for heraldry

parts.words: To do with charges for heraldry
parts.note: charges sounds like fees or accusations, but in heraldry a charge is a figure borne on a shield

explanation.surface: Something concerns the fees levied for designing coats of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: A charge is the heraldic term for a device painted on a shield, so the adjective means relating to coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to heraldic arms and the devices borne on shields.

clue.text: Sent say to find wine and Adam's ale

parts.note: rosé is pink wine
Adam's ale is a jocular name for drinking water, the only drink of the first man

explanation.surface: Someone is dispatched to fetch wine and plain water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent say' is a sound-alike definition: say 'sent' aloud and it is 'scent', and this liquid is a perfume. 'to find' and 'and' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken, 'sent' sounds like 'scent', and this fragrant liquid distilled from petals is a scent.

clue.text: Agency that sends the work to you at home

definitions.text: Agency that sends the work to you at home

parts.words: Agency that sends the work to you at home
parts.note: sounds like an outworking or employment agency, but the work is a published volume mailed to members

explanation.surface: An employment firm delivers piecework to people's homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the work' suggests a job to do; it is a literary work, a volume delivered by post to subscribers.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription scheme that mails chosen volumes to its members by post.

clue.text: Retrospective in part is outrivalling the masters

indicators.note: Retrospective says the hidden letters are read backwards
in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A retrospective exhibition shows one artist partly outshining the old masters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' hides ISOUTRIV in 'is outrivalling'; 'Retrospective', looking back, turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Masters of an art, especially music, are its brilliant performers.

clue.text: Makes a fuss of in return for advancement

indicators.note: in return says the word for fussing over someone is read backwards

parts.note: to pet someone is to make a fuss of them, so the verb form is pets

explanation.surface: Someone fawns over the boss hoping for promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion or move up is a rung gained, as in a step up the ladder.

clue.text: A mother, I. see, it's reported, with nothing on

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

indicators.note: it's reported says the next word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the word see sounds like the letter C

explanation.surface: A mother, observed and reported on, was wearing no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the first man in Eden before the fall, naked and unclothed.

clue.text: Check demand for material

parts.note: to dam a flow is to check it
to ask is to demand, as in asking a price

explanation.surface: Someone queries an invoice for fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A patterned woven fabric, originally silk from Damascus, used for tablecloths and furnishings.

clue.text: Swears. the Bible. has nothing on Shakespeare

parts.note: AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
O, the round figure nought, means nothing
WS are William Shakespeare's initials

explanation.surface: Someone declares that Shakespeare cannot match scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has nothing on' reads like 'is no better than', but 'nothing' is the letter O and 'on' only means placed after, as in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or affirm something solemnly, as under oath.

clue.text: Josiah we hear is a two-club ..man

indicators.note: we hear tells us the golf words are to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a wedge and a wood are two kinds of golf club

explanation.surface: Someone called Josiah is said to be a golfer who carries only two clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, WEDGE + WOOD gives the surname of Josiah, the 18th-century English potter, who drops the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Josiah is the first name of the famous English pottery manufacturer founder of the Staffordshire firm.

clue.text: Dimwits rarely short of food

indicators.note: short of says a letter is lost, here the opening letter of the bread

parts.note: loaves of bread are food

explanation.surface: Fools seldom go without anything to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rarely' flags that this plural of a word for a fool is the uncommon form, beside the usual one with an F.
explanation.definitionFit: Fools or clumsy louts, in a rare plural of the word for a stupid person.

clue.text: It's the hour of attack, and it's freezing!

explanation.surface: Soldiers wait in bitter cold for the moment the offensive begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The hour of attack is the military 'zero hour'; freezing point on the Celsius scale is nought degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: The fixed moment an assault begins is called this hour, and it is the Celsius reading at which water turns to ice.

clue.text: Encores demanded -by composers?

parts.note: encores are usually called for by audiences, but here the composer requires a theme to come back again and again

explanation.surface: Composers, not audiences, insist on repeat performances.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures applause; the reading is a musical theme that a composer, Wagner above all, brings back through a work.
explanation.definitionFit: These are recurring musical themes tied to a character or idea, as in Wagner's operas.

clue.text: Canon's vestment

parts.note: the outer garment a priest wears to celebrate Mass

explanation.definitionFit: This is the sleeveless outer garment worn by a priest celebrating the Eucharist.

clue.text: Mind the ship's.pet!

parts.note: to mind is to care, as in 'I don't mind'
SS, for steamship, prefixes a ship's name

explanation.surface: A warning to look after the vessel's mascot.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to stroke or fondle them tenderly.
